headline: Learned models predict genetic, proteomic, and imaging-derived disease biomarkers
label: Learned Biomarker Prediction Models
summary: Recent preprints and publications apply deep, graph, and multimodal learning to predict biomarkers from WSIs, EHRs, proteomics, and questionnaires.
synthesis: Across these items, the dominant thread is learned models that map high-dimensional or heterogeneous inputs to clinical and molecular labels, with design effort concentrated on how representations are built and combined. D2Bio uses dictionary-based hierarchical pathology mining and hard-instance-assisted debiasing to predict genetic biomarkers such as MSI from WSIs. Multimodal EHR fusion predicts metastasis a month before diagnosis across four cancer cohorts, and ProtAIDe-Dx applies deep joint learning to plasma proteomics of 17,187 individuals for six dementia-associated conditions. On the ALS study, longitudinal change descriptors from mixed-format questionnaires outperform static text-derived features. Graph-based models, SPGA and MAGMDA, address disease-associated ncRNA prediction, the latter on HMDD v2.0. What is new relative to standard supervised pipelines is explicit attention to debiasing and to temporal or multi-order structure in the inputs. The items differ in modality and maturity, so the shared thread is methodological rather than mechanistic.
